title: I tried building a SaaS for 700 days (and hit $6.7m/yr)
normalization: Concatenate utf8 segments per caption event; retain event start and duration; whitespace trim only.

segments.text: 700 days ago, I started building a new
SAS from scratch. Today, it's at 6.7
[music] million annual recurring revenue
with a team of just three people and
zero external funding. Now, this wasn't
my first rodeo. I'd already built and
exited Robblely Email Marketing for 10
million bucks, then bootstrapped
retention.com to over 20 million in ARR,
but my new company, RB2B's growth has
been unlike anything I've ever
experienced. [music] So, in this video,
I'm going to walk you through the entire
700 day journey from the painful
situation that led me to start RB2B to
hitting 1 million ARR in just 6 weeks to
the brutal challenges we faced scaling
beyond that to where we are today. Let's
dive in. So, here's the situation before
RBDB. I was running retention.com and
things were falling apart. I started
retention.com in November 2019 as a
productled growth SAS. We didn't really
know who our best customers were in the
beginning, but by mid 2022, we'd figured
out that large Shopify stores were our
ideal customer profile. So, we decided
to focus exclusively on them. Then, we
experienced the most insane product
market fit I'd ever seen. We were the
only vendor who did what we did in the
entire Shopify ecosystem. There was more
inbound demand than we had salespeople
to take demos. We were closing $30,000
deals in seven days with an 80% close
rate and we scaled to 12 million ARR
with just six people. That's when I made
a huge mistake. I hired 50 people in 60
days because I thought we were ready to
scale. I called my shot on LinkedIn and
predicted we'd triple our revenue from
15 to 45 million ARR in under one year.
Instead, we barely grew 40%. We realized
we've been overselling. Then multiple
competitors copied our offer and
undercut us substantially. I had to fire
my entire BDR team and our cold outreach
operation crashed and burned. Now most
founders would have hidden all of this.
I did the exact opposite. I started
sharing everything on LinkedIn. I talked
about the tumultuous year when my
strategy blew up in my face. I shared
the painful process of letting people go
and the real numbers behind what was
happening. People told me I was crazy
for being so transparent, but this
created the most engaged audience I'd
ever built. Now, here's how I discovered
the RB2B opportunity. While dealing with
all this chaos, I was building a
personal brand on LinkedIn. I was trying
to grow the Shopify business through
creating thought leadership content. It
worked okay, but whenever I talked about
trying to grow my SAS, the engagement
was at least 10 times higher. Other B2B
SAS founders were going through the
exact same struggles I was, but nobody
was talking about it. Then my business
partner, Santos Chiron, told me
something that changed everything. He
said, "Nobody's offering personle level
website visitor identity in the B2B
space. All the identity stops at the
company level. And there'd be massive
demand if we created a person level
product." This was the B2B version of
what we were already doing for Shopify
stores. And honestly, my favorite part
of startups is the 0 to 10 million ARR
stage. Anyway, I was kind of over all
this nonsense that was going on at
retention.com. So, I pivoted my LinkedIn
content entirely to B2B SAS on Labor Day
of 2024. Then, I had three of the most
banger posts in a row that I've ever
had. They got 1.8 million impressions
combined in just three posts. One post
talked about how we shrunk our sales
team of our 20 million AR SAS growth
actually sped up. Another said that I
bootstrapped 12 million AR with only six
people and was launching a new product.
These posts resonated because I was
being brutally honest about what wasn't
working, not just talking about what
was. Now, let's talk about validating
the idea. I started writing posts on the
shortcomings of company level
identification. And at the end of every
post, I put a simple CTA. DM me if you
want to identify your website visitors
and push their LinkedIn profiles to
Slack. It's 100% free. And I'm not
kidding. My DMs absolutely exploded.
Hundreds of messages came in from people
that wanted the product. Santosh and I
did over 300 discovery calls through
posts like this. These weren't sales
calls. They were validation calls. We
were trying to understand exactly what
people wanted and how much they paid for
it. We tried to get people to pay 495 a
month for a spreadsheet of LinkedIn URLs
and hardly anyone did it. But then we
discovered a magic moment. When we
showed people a Slack notification with
head shot and LinkedIn URLs on our
phones, their eyes lit up. I would just
show them the phone and say, "These
people just hit the retention.com
website." That was the moment we knew we
had something. I wanted to launch and be
as explosive as possible. I've always
admired Mailchimp's premium model, so we
decided to give the LinkedIn push to
Slack completely free. Competitors were
charging hundreds of thousands of
dollars, and all they did was a company
name. They didn't even ID the actual
person. Our offer was simple. Free
forever. Get LinkedIn profiles of your
anonymous website visitors pushed to
Slack. Then there was a paid tier at 149
a month that was business emails plus
access to all of the integrations other
than Slack. This generated over 1,600
weightless signups in 300 meetings in a
few months. But shortly after launch, we
hit a brutal wall. We had 3,000 signups
and only 13 paying customers. That's a
terrible conversion rate and it was
keeping me up at night. I posted about
this problem constantly on LinkedIn. The
commenters helped me figure out the
pricing and they gave me direct feedback
on exactly what it should look like. We
fixed the pricing and got to a 12.5%
touchless freeto paid conversion rate
that we're still enjoying today. That
was the unlock that we needed. After
fixing the pricing, growth exploded. We
hit 1 million ARR in just 6 weeks. This
happened during one of the hardest
periods for earlystage SAS in recent
history. Once we had organic traction,
we layered on growth accelerators. I
tapped into Clay's creator community,
exactly the people who needed our B2B.
We started doing weekly podcast
interviews and I went on a ton of guest
appearances. We turned on cold email as
well and cold email became a massive
growth driver. It drove 42% of our
entire revenue as we scaled the team
from 0 to 4 million ARR in just 6
months. We built three distinct cold
email strategies. Number one was weight
list campaigns to the 1,600 people who
signed up before launch. Number two was
pure cold outbound to US-based SAS
companies with 3 to 200 employees. The
third one was website visitor
retargeting using RB2B. And this one
converted one sign up for every 10
emails that we sent. I still can't
believe how well this worked. One sign
up for every 10 emails is like a hundred
times better than any other type of cold
email I've ever done. The whole point of
RBDB is to turn anonymous visitors into
leads you can actually talk to. And this
proved that it works. So if you want to
try it yourself, you can click the first
link below and start using RB2B. As I
said, it's completely free. After
hitting 4 million ARR, we took a pause
to fix a major product problem. We had
issues with filtering, routing, and what
we called the what now problem.
Basically, people would get a Slack
notification when someone visited their
site and they just stare at it. They
didn't know what to do next. Should they
email them? Should they connect with
them on LinkedIn? Should they wait for
another website visit? We had to build a
better integrations and workflow so
people could actually act on the data.
Plus, our churn rate was around 10%
monthly, which I'll be the first to
admit is absolutely horrible. We needed
to rebuild the product to actually
retain customers. And over time, as we
slowly fixed every problem people had
that led to them churning, churn got
lower and lower. We also started going
allin on AI. We use deli.ai to create a
clone of me that handles pre-sales
conversations on our website. Then we
use intercom Finn after the sign up and
that handles everything after people
create an account. When we started using
Finn over 2 years ago, AI was resolving
about 25% of our support inquiries. Now
AI resolves over 90% of our support
inquiries. AI is truly an amazing tool
for customer support if you build the
system correctly. Where are we today?
700 days later, this is what RB2B looks
like. 6.7 million in annual recurring
revenue, a team of just three full-time
employees, me, Rob, and Tate. zero
external funding and over 60,000 users.
AI is handling the vast majority of our
customer interactions. Over 9 out of 10.
Here's a current growth engine that
drives a business. I've gotten 16
million LinkedIn impressions over the
past 12 months. 30,000 unique visitors
per month hit the rb.com website. We get
2,000 free signups per month and 12.5%
of those convert to paid in an average
of $230 a month. Cold email still drives
around 20% of new signups and we spend
around $10,000 per month on retargeting
ads. Now, if you want to start
identifying your own website visitors
for free and replicate the outreach
strategy that got us the best results,
just click the link in the description
below and get started with RB2B today.
We'll push LinkedIn profiles of your
website visitors to Slack completely
free, just like I talked about in this
video. So again, click the link below
and get started for free. And if you
want to see how I would scale a SAS from
zero to a,000 users today, then watch
this video next.
